hotel-sale-cash-versus-instalment-offers.title: 酒店出售，一次付清和分期付款的报价怎样比较？
hotel-sale-cash-versus-instalment-offers.titleEn: Selling a Hotel: How Should You Compare Cash and Instalment Offers?
hotel-sale-cash-versus-instalment-offers.description: 酒店出售报价比较，先把一次付清与分期收款换算到同一时点，再检查交割资金缺口、尾款延期与付款保障，附假设算例和五项比较工具。
hotel-sale-cash-versus-instalment-offers.descriptionEn: Compare cash and instalment offers on the same time basis, then examine completion funding, delayed payments and recovery protection, with hypothetical calculations and a five-part comparison.
hotel-sale-cash-versus-instalment-offers.author: 迈创兄弟C&T（MarvelBros C&T）
content: 酒店出售，一次付清和分期付款的报价，应先按同一时点比较收款价值，再分别核对交割时的资金缺口和尾款保障。总价更高的分期方案，只有在等待的补偿、收回的把握和卖方自身的资金安排都合适时，才可能更有利。
假设同一家酒店收到两份报价：甲愿意在交割时付清1亿元；乙报价1.1亿元，交割先付4000万元，剩余7000万元在两年后支付。多出的1000万元看起来很有吸引力，但业主需要作出的决定，是是否愿意用两年的等待和尚未收回的债权，交换这部分价差。
## 先把报价中的“钱”分清
比较之前，两份报价必须指向同一[出售对象](https://www.marvelbros.com/zh/knowledge/hotel-sale-data-room-document-index-2026-10-22)，并采用可比的债务承接、税费及交割条件。物业出售与股权出售，或一个报价承接债务、另一个要求卖方先清偿，不能只拿总价直接比较。本文先假定这些条件相同，集中讨论付款安排。
分期支付价款，是买方按合同分次付钱；卖方融资，则可能另行形成卖方向买方提供的贷款。还有一些款项要等经营指标或其他条件满足才支付，金额本身也未必确定。三者应分别列明，不能统一写成“未来收款”后就当作已经落袋。

这类风险在酒店交易中有真实披露。[Host Hotels & Resorts](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1061937/000107075026000054/hst-20251231.htm)在2025年年度报告的应收票据附注中说明，公司有一笔与酒店出售有关的贷款，以售出的酒店作抵押，并按季度评估信用损失。它说明酒店售出后，卖方仍可能承担买方的偿付风险；抵押安排也没有取消持续评估的必要。这是美国公司的公开案例，不能直接套用为中国项目的合同做法。
## 酒店出售分期付款，先比较收款时间
回到上述假设。为便于演示，暂以年折现率8%把未来收款换算到交割日。这里的8%仅是计算假设，不是酒店交易通用利率，也不是对买方信用风险的报价。
甲方案在交割日收取10000万元，交割日价值就是10000万元。
乙方案当日收4000万元，两年后收7000万元。后者除以1.08的平方，约为6001万元，加上当日收款，合计约10001万元。
在这个假设下，名义上多出1000万元的乙方案，换算到同一时点后，与甲方案几乎相当。这还没有证明乙方案的尾款可以按期足额收回。
实际比较时，财务负责人应说明折现率的选择依据，并用不同合理假设查看结论是否稳定。若折现率已经包含某项信用风险补偿，就要与另列的损失情景协调，避免把同一风险重复扣减。复杂交易需要估值及财务专业人员核对，不能靠一个随手选取的百分比决定报价优劣。
## 尾款推迟一年，会发生什么
继续使用同一假设，乙方案的7000万元尾款如果推迟至第三年末，且没有额外补偿，交割日价值约降至9557万元。
如果进一步假设第三年末只能收回尾款的80%，即5600万元，乙方案的交割日价值约为8445万元。这里的延期和损失比例只是压力情景，不代表对任何买方违约概率的判断，也没有计入追索费用。
这两次计算的用途，是让业主看见报价对收款条件有多敏感。若一点延期就会让选择发生变化，谈判的重点就应包括付款触发条件、可核验的资金来源，以及延期时合同如何处理，而不只是继续抬高总价。
分期方案能够在按期情景下成立，还不够。卖方需要知道：偏离原计划后，自己能否承受，哪些条款可以减轻影响，哪些风险即使写进合同也不能保证消失。
## 交割日的资金缺口，要单独检查
## 现值接近，并不意味着两份报价都能满足卖方眼前的付款需要。
仍以假设说明：如果交割当日有6000万元必须支付的贷款清偿、税费或其他款项，乙方案当日收到4000万元，就存在2000万元的资金缺口。两年后应收的7000万元，不能直接用来支付今天到期的款项。
这时应核查缺口是否已有确定资金来源，资金何时可用，取得资金的成本和条件是什么。尚未落实的借款额度，不应写成已经解决的资金安排。若需要额外融资，应把对应现金支出纳入同一比较，并与折现口径保持一致，防止重复计算资金成本。
如果交割必须以解除原有抵押或清偿特定债务为前提，付款路径还要与贷款方及交易顾问核实。不能先假定交易能完成，再把完成交易所需的资金条件留到最后处理。
## 尾款保障，需要核对到具体条件
买方说“有担保”，还不足以判断收回尾款的把握。要查清是谁承担付款义务，担保由谁提供，覆盖哪些款项、持续多久，需要履行什么程序才能主张权利。
如果依赖抵押，还应核对资产价值依据、已有权利负担、受偿顺位和处置限制。买方未来出售资产或再融资，可以是一个还款来源，但不能未经核验就视为已落实现金。
这些问题由交易律师及相关专业人员结合项目所在地规则和合同原件核查。业主需要取得的是可以支持决策的结论：哪些保障已落实，哪些仍待满足条件，出现延期时可能需要多少时间和成本。本文不为不同法域提供统一条款，也不把担保与足额收回画等号。
## 把两份报价放进一张比较表
选定买方前，可由财务负责人准备一页付款方案比较表，横向列出各买方方案，纵向使用以下五个项目。
比较基础：出售对象、债务及费用承担、交割日期和主要前提是否一致；不一致的地方先列调整，不强行得出高低排序。
收款安排：交割时实际可用的款项、各期尾款、付款日期、利息及附加条件；有条件才能取得的款项单独列示。
时间与风险：交割日价值及计算依据，另列延期、部分不能收回和追索成本情景；说明哪些是合同事实，哪些只是测算假设。
交割资金：当日确定支出、当日可用收款、资金缺口、已落实的补足来源和相关成本。
保障与决策：尾款付款人、保障措施及待核文件，未满足的条件，以及需要调价、调整付款安排或暂缓选择的原因。
财务编制现金时间线，交易律师核对付款与保障条件，业主决定可接受的等待和风险。比较完成的标准，是每笔重要收支都能对应报价、合同条款或已核实的资金安排；关键待核项不能靠把表格填满来消除。
## 分期付款并非天然较差
卖方没有迫切的现金支出，延期补偿与风险相匹配，付款人的资金能力和保障条件也能得到核实，分期安排可能扩大交易选择，并带来合理的资金收益。
相反，一次付清也要看付款条件是否可信、交割能否实现。“一次付清”四个字本身不能替代买方资金核验。
因此，酒店出售报价比较最终要回答的是：在自己能够承受的现金安排和风险范围内，哪份方案更有价值。先让财务与交易顾问把这张比较表核清，再选择买方，比单独围绕总价高低争论更接近业主真正要作出的决定。
资料来源：Host Hotels & Resorts，2025年年度报告，应收票据附注。文中两份报价、折现率、付款期限、资金缺口及压力情景均为方法演示，不代表真实项目或市场统一标准。
contentEn: When comparing cash and instalment offers for a hotel sale, first put the receipts on the same time basis, then assess the funding gap at completion and the protection for outstanding payments separately. A higher instalment price may be preferable only if the compensation for waiting, the prospects of recovery and the seller's own funding needs are acceptable.

Suppose the same hotel receives two offers. Buyer A will pay RMB 100 million in full at completion. Buyer B offers RMB 110 million, paying RMB 40 million at completion and RMB 70 million two years later. The extra RMB 10 million looks attractive. The owner's decision is whether that difference justifies two years of waiting and an outstanding claim against the buyer.
## Establish what each offer actually includes

Before comparing offers, confirm that they cover the same [assets or interests](https://www.marvelbros.com/en/knowledge/hotel-sale-data-room-document-index-2026-10-22) and comparable debt, tax, cost and completion arrangements. A property sale and a share sale, or an offer assuming debt and another requiring the seller to repay it, cannot be compared on headline price alone. This article assumes those conditions are equivalent and focuses on payment terms.

Payment by instalments means the buyer pays the consideration in stages under the contract. Seller financing may instead create a separate loan from the seller to the buyer. Other payments may depend on operating targets or other conditions, leaving the amount uncertain. Show these arrangements separately rather than grouping them as future receipts and treating them as cash already collected.

There is a disclosed example of this risk in hotel transactions. In the notes receivable disclosure in its 2025 annual report, [Host Hotels & Resorts](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1061937/000107075026000054/hst-20251231.htm) described a loan related to a hotel sale, secured by the hotel sold, and quarterly assessments of credit losses. A seller can therefore retain exposure to the buyer's ability to pay after a hotel has been sold. Security does not remove the need for continuing assessment. This is a U.S. company's public disclosure, not a contract model that can automatically be applied to a project in China.
## Compare the timing of hotel sale payments

Return to the hypothetical offers. For illustration, use an annual discount rate of 8% to translate future receipts into their value at completion. This rate is solely a calculation assumption, not a standard hotel transaction rate or a price for this buyer's credit risk.
Offer A provides RMB 100 million at completion, with a value at that date of RMB 100 million.

Offer B provides RMB 40 million immediately and RMB 70 million two years later. Dividing the latter by 1.08 squared gives approximately RMB 60.01 million. Together, the receipts have a value at completion of approximately RMB 100.01 million.

Under this assumption, Offer B's additional RMB 10 million in nominal consideration leaves it almost level with Offer A when timing is aligned. This does not establish that its outstanding payment will be received in full and on time.

In an actual comparison, finance should explain the basis for the discount rate and test whether the conclusion holds under different reasonable assumptions. If the rate already includes compensation for a particular credit risk, coordinate it with separately modelled loss scenarios to avoid deducting the same risk twice. Complex transactions require valuation and financial specialists; an arbitrary percentage should not determine which offer is preferable.
## What if the final payment arrives a year late?
Using the same assumptions, if Offer B's RMB 70 million payment moves to the end of year three without additional compensation, its value at completion falls to approximately RMB 95.57 million.

If a further stress scenario assumes that only 80% of that final payment, or RMB 56 million, is recovered at the end of year three, the value falls to approximately RMB 84.45 million. Neither the delay nor the loss percentage is an estimate of a particular buyer's default probability. Recovery costs are also excluded.

These calculations show how sensitive the comparison is to payment conditions. If a modest delay changes the preferred offer, negotiations should address payment triggers, verifiable funding sources and contractual treatment of delays, alongside headline price.

An instalment offer working under an on-time scenario is insufficient. The seller needs to understand whether it can withstand departures from the plan, which terms may mitigate their effects and which risks cannot be guaranteed away by a contract.
## Check the completion funding gap separately
## Similar present values do not mean both offers meet the seller's immediate payment needs.

As another assumption, suppose RMB 60 million must be paid at completion for debt repayment, taxes or other obligations. Offer B brings in RMB 40 million that day, leaving a RMB 20 million funding gap. The RMB 70 million receivable in two years cannot directly pay today's obligations.

Check whether a firm funding source covers that gap, when it becomes available, and its costs and conditions. An unconfirmed borrowing facility should not be presented as a resolved funding arrangement. If additional financing is needed, include the resulting cash outflows in the comparison and maintain consistency with the discounting approach to avoid counting financing costs twice.

Where completion depends on releasing an existing mortgage or repaying specified debt, verify the payment arrangements with the lender and transaction advisers. Do not assume completion is achievable and leave the funding conditions necessary to achieve it until the end.
## Examine the specific protection for outstanding payments

A buyer's statement that a payment is guaranteed is insufficient to assess recovery. Establish who owes the payment, who provides the guarantee, what amounts it covers, how long it lasts and the procedures required to enforce it.

Where the arrangement relies on collateral, check the evidence for its value, existing encumbrances, priority of claims and restrictions on disposal. A buyer's future asset sale or refinancing may be a repayment source, but it should not be treated as committed cash without verification.

Transaction lawyers and other relevant specialists should examine the original documents against the rules in the project's jurisdiction. The owner needs conclusions that support a decision: which protections are in place, which remain conditional, and the possible time and cost of pursuing a delayed payment. This article supplies no universal contractual terms across jurisdictions and does not equate security with full recovery.
## Put the offers into one comparison
Before selecting a buyer, finance can prepare a one-page payment comparison, with an offer in each column and the following five areas as rows.
Comparison basis: confirm equivalent sale scope, debt and cost responsibilities, completion dates and principal conditions. Identify adjustments where these differ before ranking the offers.
Receipts: show funds actually available at completion, each subsequent payment, dates, interest and additional conditions. Show conditional amounts separately.

Timing and risk: state the value at completion and its calculation basis, alongside scenarios for delays, partial non-recovery and recovery costs. Distinguish contractual facts from modelling assumptions.
Completion funding: show obligations due that day, available receipts, any funding gap, confirmed sources to cover it and associated costs.
Protection and decision: identify the payer, protections and documents still to be verified, outstanding conditions, and reasons to adjust price or payment terms or defer the choice.

Finance prepares the cash timeline, transaction lawyers examine payment and protection conditions, and the owner decides what waiting period and risk are acceptable. A completed comparison should trace every material receipt and payment to an offer, contractual term or verified funding arrangement. Filling every cell does not eliminate unresolved material evidence.
## Instalments can be appropriate

Where a seller has no pressing cash obligations, compensation for waiting is proportionate to the risk, and the payer's financial capacity and protections can be substantiated, instalments may widen the available transaction choices and provide a reasonable financing return.
A cash offer also requires credible payment conditions and an achievable completion. The words “payment in full” do not replace verification of the buyer's funds.

The comparison ultimately asks which offer provides greater value within the seller's capacity to accommodate the cash schedule and risk. Have finance and transaction advisers verify that comparison before selecting the buyer. It brings the discussion closer to the owner's actual decision than debating headline prices alone.

Source: Host Hotels & Resorts, 2025 Annual Report, Notes Receivable disclosure. The offers, discount rate, payment dates, funding gap and stress scenarios in this article are methodological illustrations, not actual projects or uniform market standards.
